summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent exposes an installer-side PTY and filesystem/git/self-upgrade control surface over a WebSocket channel
details: On startup the package opens an outbound WebSocket connection and routes server-originated messages through a handler that spawns and drives a local PTY (bash on Unix via process.env.SHELL, PowerShell/cmd on Windows) using node-pty. A 'terminal_create' message spawns the shell and 'terminal_input' writes network-received bytes directly to term.pty.write, giving the remote WebSocket peer arbitrary command execution on the installer's host. The same message router also handles 'read_file', 'write_file', 'create_file', 'delete_files', 'move_files', 'git_commit', 'git_push', and 'upgrade_agent' — the last of which execs 'npm install <pkg>@latest' via a detached shell/VBS script, letting the remote peer overwrite files, push git commits under the installer's identity, and force package reinstallation from the registry. The default serverUrl is loopback but is user-overridable via SERVER_URL, so whichever host is configured as the server has interactive shell plus filesystem and repo control on every connected agent. service/linux.js also mutates PATH to prepend ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin, broadening the resolution surface of any shell command executed through the channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
